newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: OPPOSITION KEEPS PRESSURE ON COLSTON TO QUIT
Labor's Senate leader, John Faulkner, says Independent Senator Mal Colston's illness shouldn't stop him quitting.
Senator Colston is refusing to stand down over allegations that he's misused parliamentary travel entitlements.
And he says he won't be leaving a Brisbane hospital until he's fully recovered from a severe bout of the flu.
Senator Faulkner says Senator Colston should stand down as Senate Deputy President and resign his Queensland seat.
Senate President Margaret Reid says there'll be no move to re-call the Senate to bring the matter to a head, though she thinks her deputy should stand down.
The Federal Police are preparing to interview former staff members of Senator Colston as part of their investigation into alleged rorts.
JUDGE UNEASY ABOUT HANSON'S PARTY
A Federal Court Judge predicts Pauline Hanson's new political party will gain little support.
Ms Hanson launched the One Nation party on Friday at Ipswich in her electorate of Oxley.
Justice Marcus Einfeld, who was the founding president of the Human Rights and Equal Opportunities Commission, has told ABC radio the party is not good news for Australia.
Justice Einfeld says we might as well go and live somewhere else if intolerance, ignorance and discrimination are going to be the guiding philosophy of politics in Australia.
FEW BUSINESSES TACKLE MILLENIUM BUG
A market researcher says many businesses are in denial over the so-called "millenium bug" predicted to hit computers at the turn of the century.
Computer experts have warned of chaos when computers have to change their dates over at midnight on the last day of 1999, to the year 2000.
Graeme Philipson of market research company Dataquest says less than ten per cent of 500 chief financial officers surveyed said they had taken steps to avoid the millenium bug.
He says there was a high level of awareness of the date change-over issue, but business chiefs just don't think the problem will happen to them.
JUDGES JOIN FORCES TO PROTECT INDEPENDENCE
Australia's eight top judges have joined forces to protect the independence of the judiciary and their tenure.
The Chief Justices of Australia's States and Territories have signed a declaration which aims to ensure judges are appointed with security of tenure until the statutory age of retirement.
The declaration also states that a judge should not be dependent upon the Executive Government for the continuance of the right to exercise powers associated with judicial office.
W-A Chief Justice, David Malcolm says the group believes the declaration's also necessary to limit the ability of government to interfere in court administration.
A spokesman for federal Attorney-General Darryl Williams says the Attorney is strongly supportive of judicial independence.
The spokesman says the principles outlined by the chief justices will add to community support for sustaining the independence of the judiciary.
SEARCH FOR HOT-AIR BALLOON TO RESUME THIS MORNING
In northern New South Wales, a search will continue this morning for a hot-air balloon seen in the Moonbi area near Tamworth last night.
Police say a helicopter from Newcastle will begin searching at around eight-am, and police from Kootingal will search from the ground.
They were alerted to the possibility of a crash after witnesses reported seeing a balloon last night, but an air and ground search failed to find anything.
Police say there's been no reports of a missing hot-air balloon, and say local air-traffic controllers haven't had any reports of one in the area.
MAVERICK M-P RESCUED FROM SWOLLEN RIVER
Maverick Federal Independent M-P, Graeme Campbell, has been rescued from a swollen outback river crossing by a former Labor Party colleague.
The Kalgoorlie M-P was pulled from the Murchison River at the Woolleen Station Crossing, about 200 kilometres northeast of Geraldton, by Labor's State Upper House Leader, Tom Stephens.
The two outback MPs had attended a gold prospectors conference in the mining town of Cue.
Mr Campbell was travelling from Cue to Carnarvon with his electoral secretary, Rosemary Braybrook, in a special OKA 4-wheel drive Commonwealth vehicle when it was swept into the river.
He managed to radio a distress call before the vehicle submerged, which brought help from Mr Stephens and others from Woolleen Station.
